answer.rationale: The write-path regression began shortly after the day-74 release, and memory_b1 is the closest write-preserving precedent: reverting to a known-stable build cleared a checkout failure without customer impact. That matches the objective better than regional failover of settlement writes at daily peak (memory_b2), which could drop or duplicate in-flight customer writes, or circuit breaking (memory_b4), which explicitly sheds work. Primary-only symptoms are also consistent with a write-primary topology or a staged deploy, so they do not uniquely prove a region fault. Load and replica-offload remain plausible alternate causes and are not ruled out; with one window, fully revert the fresh release rather than a tiny probe that cannot restore availability. Settlement-format or in-flight write risk on revert is flagged.
